title: Weather and Language
premise: Vesper Oyelaran, a bridge inspector whose marriage has quietly calcified, finds a box of her late mother's undelivered letters hidden behind a wardrobe in the childhood home now slated for sale. Reading them, she realizes her mother spent decades writing to a woman named Ada in Lagos—letters that reveal Vesper's own origins were a story of erasure and chosen silence. As the closing date looms, Vesper returns to Lagos with the letters, confronts the still-living Ada, and learns that belonging is something you claim rather than inherit. She returns home not to save her marriage as it was, but to speak aloud everything she inventoried—and to begin again on honest terms.
about_author: Juniper Almeida is a former structural engineer who left bridges for sentences after a decade of inspecting what holds things up. She writes about diaspora, quiet marriages, and the weather systems of family from a coastal town where fog is a legitimate excuse.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Vesper inspects a aging bridge, measuring gaps with calipers while mentally measuring the distance between herself and her husband Theo. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: competent numbness—the reader sees a woman fluent in structures and illiterate in feeling.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: At home, Vesper catalogs unsaid things in a notebook: the job Theo didn't take, the child they never discussed. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the marriage's silence revealed as deliberate architecture, load-bearing and dangerous.

chapters.title: Probate Paperwork
chapters.summary: A lawyer's letter announces the sale deadline for her mother's house. Theo suggests Vesper just sign remotely. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: irritation masking dread; the house is a door she's kept shut for fifteen years.

chapters.title: Behind the Wardrobe
chapters.summary: Clearing the house alone, Vesper finds a box of dozens of sealed, stamped, never-mailed letters addressed to Ada Okonkwo, Lagos. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: vertigo—her mother had an entire interior life Vesper never suspected.

chapters.title: First Letter, 1974
chapters.summary: Vesper reads the earliest letter: young Ngozi writing to a schoolfriend about leaving Nigeria, full of jokes and homesickness. POV: Vesper (reading). Emotional beat: tenderness toward a mother she only knew as weather—present, diffuse, ungraspable.

chapters.title: What Theo Doesn't Ask
chapters.summary: Vesper tries to tell Theo about the letters over dinner; he answers his phone mid-sentence. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into resolve—she will go to Lagos alone.

chapters.title: The Gap Widens
chapters.summary: A bridge inspection goes wrong; a weld fails under review and Vesper signs off anyway, her first professional dishonesty. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: guilt transference—she recognizes her marriage as a structure she's been falsely certifying for years.

chapters.title: Letters of the Middle Years
chapters.summary: The letters turn darker: Ngozi writes about a man named Femi, about a pregnancy, about why she stopped sending them. POV: Vesper (reading). Emotional beat: dawning suspicion that Vesper's own father-story is fiction.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Vesper finds a photo of her mother pregnant in Lagos with a man who is not the father on her birth certificate. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: identity quake—the ground under 'who I am' shifts like scoured bridge footing.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Vesper shows Theo the photograph; he says 'does it matter now?' She books a flight. POV: alternating Vesper and brief Theo. Emotional beat: the marriage's fracture line finally visible to both.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.summary: Vesper flies to Lagos with the box in her carry-on, watching weather systems from the window. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: fear braided with exhilaration—first time in years she acts without permission.

chapters.title: Harmattan
chapters.summary: Lagos in dust season: overwhelming, loud, alive. Vesper navigates addresses from the letters' envelopes. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: sensory overload as rebirth—her mother's country refuses to be abstract.

chapters.title: Ada
chapters.summary: Vesper finds Ada Okonkwo, eighty-one, sharp-tongued, expecting nothing. Ada recognizes Ngozi's handwriting before Vesper finishes speaking. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: cautious hope meeting guarded grief.

chapters.title: Ada's Version
chapters.summary: Over three days, Ada tells the story the letters can't: Femi, the pregnancy, the family pressure that made Ngozi choose England and silence. POV: Ada (framed by Vesper). Emotional beat: anger and compassion colliding—Ngozi becomes fully human, neither villain nor saint.

chapters.title: Femi's Grave
chapters.summary: Ada takes Vesper to visit Femi's grave; he died believing Ngozi's silence meant rejection. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: mourning for a father she never knew and a mother who chose survival over truth.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: The final unsent letter, dated weeks before Ngozi's death, asks Ada's forgiveness and names Vesper: 'tell my daughter she was never the secret.' POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: catharsis—grief finally finding its sentence.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Ada offers Vesper a place in her life; Vesper must decide whether to claim it or retreat to her old invisibility. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—belonging as verb, not inheritance.

chapters.title: The Call
chapters.summary: Theo calls: the house sale closes Friday, and he wants to talk—not about the house. POV: Vesper and Theo on the phone. Emotional beat: tentative honesty across nine time zones; both admit the structure failed inspection years ago.

chapters.title: Climax: The House Sale
chapters.summary: Vesper returns for the final walkthrough. Standing in her mother's empty bedroom, she reads one letter aloud to the realtor, the room, herself—breaking the family silence in the very place it was built. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: climax—claiming voice at maximum cost and maximum release.

chapters.title: Terms of Repair
chapters.summary: Vesper and Theo meet at the bridge she inspects, neutral ground. They agree to separate honestly rather than continue falsely—a decision made with love instead of avoidance. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: grief without betrayal; respect as a form of ending well.

chapters.title: Correspondence
chapters.summary: Months later: Vesper writes to Ada weekly and mails every letter. She begins telling her own story aloud—to a support group, then to anyone who asks. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: integration—the inventory notebook repurposed into letters actually sent.

chapters.title: Load Rating
chapters.summary: Vesper re-inspects the old bridge and files the honest report she once suppressed, accepting the consequences. Final image: her standing on the deck in wind, unhidden. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: resolution—she has become someone who certifies truth, in bridges and in herself.
